cargo_lock_status.reason: This wave adds no new dependencies; it only edits existing modules to fold already-produced extraction results into the canonical census path and to isolate read failures.

ci_status_detail: GitHub Actions assigns no runner at all, reproducing identically on main across every prior R4 wave (R4.1/R4.2/R4.2.1/R4.2.2/R4.3 evidence records document the same root cause). Not a test/code failure; excluded from correctness verification per operator instruction.

architectural_defect_fixed.old_runtime_flow: systemize(): build_census(inventory, source, adl) [hardcoded UNSUPPORTED coverage for all 12 R4 dimensions] -> normalize -> graph; THEN, separately, extract_semantics(...) ran the real RustSemanticExtractor and discarded every SemanticObservation/ObligationResult after only computing a single closure boolean fed into coding_admission.blockers. Real extraction never reached CensusReport.facts, so normalize()/build_system_graph() were never actually downstream of what the extractor produced -- an accounting-only sidecar next to, not inside, the one normalized semantic path.
architectural_defect_fixed.new_runtime_flow: systemize()/graph()/code_analyze(): extraction_batches = extract_semantics(...) runs FIRST; census = build_census(inventory, source, adl, &extraction_batches) folds every SemanticObservation into a typed SemanticFactKind (Symbol/Type/FunctionIdentity/FunctionSignature) fact and every ObligationResult into a per-artifact SemanticObligation fact, and derives CensusReport.coverage from that same data (most-informative-status-wins) instead of a hardcoded literal; normalize(&census) and build_system_graph(...) then run on that same CensusReport. CensusExtractionAccounting (for the closure blocker) is built from the identical extraction_batches slice census was built from, so closure accounting and canonical census truth can never disagree.

read_failure_isolation_fixed.old_behavior: extract_semantics used `fs::read_to_string(root.join(&artifact.path))?` -- a single unreadable artifact (removed after inventory admission, permission denied, invalid UTF-8, ...) propagated an io::Error out of the whole function via `?`, silently aborting extraction of every artifact enumerated after it in inventory.artifacts.
read_failure_isolation_fixed.new_behavior: extract_semantics is now infallible (returns Vec<ExtractionBatch> directly). A read failure is caught per-artifact via a match/Err arm, which builds an ExtractionDiagnostic(DiagnosticCode::InvalidInput) and calls the new SemanticExtractor::unavailable(...) default trait method for every registered extractor for that artifact's language, producing a closed batch (every supported dimension UNKNOWN, every unsupported dimension UNSUPPORTED) before continuing the loop -- never a silent drop, never an abort of later artifacts.
read_failure_isolation_fixed.distinguishability: The read-failure diagnostic uses DiagnosticCode::InvalidInput; a parser-level failure (unchanged, pre-existing) uses DiagnosticCode::ParseFailure. Both share EpistemicStatus::Unknown (evidence was insufficient either way) but the underlying cause is preserved via the distinct diagnostic code, never collapsed into one undifferentiated state.
read_failure_isolation_fixed.proof: New test a_read_failure_on_a_middle_artifact_never_aborts_or_erases_the_batch (runtime/src/census/extraction.rs) constructs an inventory of [a.rs (readable), b.rs (admitted but never written to disk), c.rs (readable)] and asserts: all 3 artifacts produce a batch; a.rs and c.rs SYMBOL obligations are OBSERVED; b.rs SYMBOL obligation is UNKNOWN with an InvalidInput diagnostic (never ParseFailure); b.rs's OWNERSHIP obligation is still UNSUPPORTED; the whole accounting is_closed().

runtime_invariants_established: No semantic observation Atlas treats as census truth can bypass CensusReport -- every ExtractionBatch passed to build_census is folded into census.facts before normalize/graph run.

No graph semantic fact exists solely because an extractor sidecar emitted it -- the engineering graph is built from NormalizationReport.facts, which is built from CensusReport.facts, which now genuinely includes real extraction output.

No supported extraction failure (read failure or parse failure) can silently remove an artifact from census accounting -- both failure modes produce an explicit, closed ExtractionBatch with UNKNOWN obligations, never a dropped artifact.

Closure accounting (CensusExtractionAccounting.is_closed) and canonical census truth (CensusReport) are built from the identical extraction_batches slice in every production entry point (systemize/graph/code_analyze), so they cannot structurally disagree.
